skill.name: model-discovery
skill.description: Fetch current AI model names from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama, then map them to fast, default, and heavy tiers.
skill.summary: Discover current AI model IDs and tier them for agent routing.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate model-discovery intent and no prompt-injection language was found. The main security concerns are executable refresh scripts that read API keys, load .env files, run curl subprocesses, and contact provider endpoints. Most Markdown and configuration findings are documentation false positives, but command examples and script paths create real credential-handling risk.

remediation.issue: Provider API keys are passed to curl command-line arguments or query strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use a Python HTTP client or provider SDK so credentials stay in request headers and are not exposed through process arguments.

remediation.issue: The fetch script searches parent directories for .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicit skill-local configuration file or require users to pass a specific dotenv path.

remediation.issue: Normal workflows can trigger network requests from agent instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before forced refreshes and document the exact provider domains contacted.

remediation.issue: The SKILL.md example writes to a predictable /tmp/new_models.json path.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or a skill-owned cache path with safe permissions for temporary output.

semantic_findings.title: API Keys Exposed Through Curl Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The fetch script passes provider API keys to curl as command-line headers or URL query parameters. Those expanded secrets can be visible in local process metadata, logs, or diagnostic output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly builds curl invocations containing API key material in arguments or URLs. This is a clear credential-exposure risk even though the endpoints are legitimate providers.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Parent Directory Dotenv Loading
semantic_findings.description: The script searches upward from its location for a .env file and loads the first match. This can import unintended parent-project secrets before provider API requests run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code walks parent directories and calls load_dotenv on the discovered file, then falls back to default dotenv loading. The risk is contextual because provider secrets are consumed afterward.

content.value_statement: Model names change quickly and stale IDs break agent workflows. This skill fetches provider model lists, caches them, and maps them into routing tiers.
actual_capabilities: Fetches model lists from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and local Ollama endpoints.
Caches provider responses in cache/models.json with a 24 hour freshness window.
Maps models into fast, default, and heavy tiers using config/model_tiers.json.
Detects new unclassified models and reports which provider returned them.
Can auto-classify common model names by patterns such as mini, flash, pro, and opus.
Includes provider cookbooks with endpoints, response fields, and troubleshooting notes.
limitations: Cloud provider discovery requires API keys configured in environment variables or a .env file.
The OpenAI fetcher filters results to the GPT-5.2 family only.
Tier mappings can become stale unless refreshed and reviewed regularly.
The scripts use curl subprocesses, so restricted environments may block execution.

use_cases.title: Refresh Agent Model References
use_cases.description: Check current provider model IDs before updating prompts, routing rules, or skill documentation.

use_cases.title: Classify Newly Released Models
use_cases.description: Detect models missing from the registry and assign them to fast, default, or heavy tiers.

use_cases.title: Select Local Ollama Models
use_cases.description: List installed local models and compare their size, parameters, and suitability for coding tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch One Provider
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner refresh for a single provider.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use model-discovery to fetch the latest OpenAI model IDs. Explain any missing API key or network error in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Check New Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Use model-discovery to check whether any provider returned new unclassified models. Summarize the count by provider and suggested tier.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Routing Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the current tier configuration and recommend fast, default, and heavy model choices for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Model Registry Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare cached provider results with known models, identify stale tier mappings, and propose registry updates without changing files automatically.

output_examples.input: Check for new OpenAI models and tell me what changed.
output_examples.output: The OpenAI registry has two new GPT-5.2 family models. One looks fast, and one looks heavy. Both need review before production use.

output_examples.input: Which Claude model should I use for a quick code formatting task?
output_examples.output: Use the fast Claude tier for quick formatting. The current mapping points to the Haiku class in the Claude Code CLI.

output_examples.input: Refresh all provider data, but do not modify tier files.
output_examples.output: The provider data was refreshed and cached. No tier files were changed. Review the new model report before saving classifications.

best_practices: Run discovery with the narrowest provider option needed for the task.
Review new model classifications before using them in production routing.
Keep provider API keys scoped and avoid sharing cache files outside the project.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode model IDs from memory when current provider data is available.
Do not run forced refreshes in untrusted workspaces with broad .env files.
Do not treat auto-classified models as production ready without review.

faq.question: Does this skill call external APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The fetch script can call Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama endpoints when refreshing model data.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Where are discovered models stored?
faq.answer: Fetched provider responses are cached in cache/models.json. Known classifications are stored in config/known_models.json.

faq.question: Can it classify models automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses name patterns to infer fast, default, or heavy tiers, then reports models that still need review.

faq.question: Does it need API keys?
faq.answer: Cloud providers need API keys. Ollama discovery uses the configured local host and does not require a provider key.

faq.question: Is it safe to run in a locked-down environment?
faq.answer: It may be blocked by network, subprocess, filesystem, or environment access restrictions.
